We have carbon NMR peaks: 9 signals. Need number of methyl groups (CH3). Methyl carbon appears around 10-30 ppm typically. Here we have peaks at 43.30 and 26.29. 43 ppm could be a carbon attached to heteroatom (e.g., carbonyl adjacent). 26.29 is typical for methyl. Also maybe other low-field? No other low ppm. So likely one methyl group. But need confirm if any other methyl carbon hidden at 43? 43 is more like CH2 next to carbonyl or aromatic. So answer 1.

Check if any other data? Could also use proton NMR to see methyl signals. Let's get proton NMR.
